speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) since the deployment of surveillance cameras by NEA to address the high-rise littering problem, how many of those caught were repeat offenders; and (b) whether the Ministry will look into further measures to deter such offences and explore further use of technology to bring such offenders to task.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the trend of high-rise littering over the last three years; (b) how effective have NEA's enforcement actions been in arresting the culprits; and (c) whether there are plans to further improve the high-rise littering situation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) whether the situation of high-rise littering in housing estates has worsened; and (b) whether there can be a greater deterrence if the public is able to report and submit visual evidence to NEA similar to how the public can now report errant PMD users.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) in the past year, how many reports from the public have been received and how many of such reports have resulted in prosecution of the culprit on environmental issues, such as littering and dumping; (b) what is the standard protocol for NEA to handle such reports; and (c) when the identity of the perpetrator is known, how long will enforcement action take.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Enforcement action is taken when there is substantiated evidence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To this end, NEA first assesses whether sufficient leads are available from the feedback before investigating further.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As part of the investigation process, NEA may interview witnesses and suspects, and conduct stakeouts and patrols to identify the offender and ascertain culpability.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Cameras may also be deployed, where feasible, to monitor the situation and aid investigations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Once sufficient evidence against the offender is collected, enforcement action will be taken.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Depending on the complexity of the case and the response time of the feedback provider and suspected offender, this process generally takes between 10 weeks to six months for most cases.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These figures have remained relatively stable over the past few years, hovering between 2,300 and 2,800 each year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In most cases, the situation improved following outreach efforts conducted by NEA, Town Councils and grassroots organisations to caution residents against committing such acts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: However, there are some who persist with such inconsiderate acts despite our education efforts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To address this, NEA has, since 2012, deployed surveillance cameras with video analytics to catch offenders in the act.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These cameras have contributed significantly to improving NEA’s enforcement effort.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Stiff penalties are in place to deter high-rise littering.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First-time offenders can be fined up to $2,000 for each offence, whilst recalcitrant offenders face fines of up to $10,000 or Corrective Work Order (CWO) in addition to, or in lieu of, a fine upon conviction.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last year, about 2,600 CWOs were issued for all littering offences.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Since May this year, NEA has also introduced standees with CWO-related information during CWO sessions and revamped the design of the CWO vest which offenders don to raise public awareness about CWO, increasing the deterrent effect.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The public can report high-rise littering offences through various channels.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members of the public can call NEA's hotline or submit information or evidence of an offence, such as photos and video footage, through the myENV mobile application.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: While we have laws to deter littering and other environmental offences, it is more important that we foster collective responsibility for our environment and cultivate positive social norms.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To this end, NEA has been working closely with the Public Hygiene Council and partners of the "Keep Singapore Clean" movement to inculcate the habit of keeping our homes and neighbourhoods clean.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Significant resources are devoted to engaging a wide range of stakeholders, including residents, schools, communities, grassroots organisations, private and public organisations, as well as foreign workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many of them conduct ground-up activities, such as litter-picking activities, beach and park clean-ups, and cleaner appreciation days, reflecting the whole-of-society approach needed to keep our public places clean.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Residents should also bin their litter properly and contact their Town Councils for assistance in disposing of bulky waste items if they are staying in public estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government will continue with our efforts to develop greater environmental stewardship, but we cannot do it alone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Every one of us must do our part to keep Singapore a clean, green and sustainable home for our future generations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: My residents have complained about high-rise littering but, somehow or other, the solution does not seem to be there.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I wonder, of the 52 repeat offenders, how many did NEA refer to the CWO.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Would NEA be open to working with the Housing and Development Board (HDB) to repossess the flats of recalcitrant high-rise litterers because, really, they pose a danger to the rest of the residents who are just there waiting to be hurt.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The recent incident whereby a man died due to high-rise littering, that is something that is cause for concern for many innocent people who are walking around on the ground floor wondering whether a "missile" from above will hit them.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I hope NEA can clarify and impose a stricter punishment against those who are recalcitrant.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, of course, a CWO can be issued.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I do not have specific numbers of the 52 repeat offenders that had gone for CWO.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I would assume it is quite a number, but I can give the specific number to the Member separately.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards to working with HDB, actually there are provisions under the HDB legislation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But these are extreme measures and we really need to consider all factors before the relevant authority can make a decision on this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, I would not say that definitely this is an avenue that we will take, but it is something that is an available option, depending on the factors of the case, such as, if it is killer litter, it is under the Penal Code, and the Police will investigate and it is even harsher penalties.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State whether NEA can also have that kind of resources and, hence, the efficacy and urgency to deal with some of these situations, some of which are actually fatal near misses as well?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With that kind of capabilities, they can better deter as well as increase the chances of catching litter bugs at our estates.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me say that I offer my condolences to the family of the victim who passed away due to killer-litter at Spottiswoode 18 condominium.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the length of time we take to investigate, which is what the Member is asking about, as the Member has rightly pointed out, we need to take prompt action.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, we also need to make sure that our investigations are thorough and accurate so that we do not wrongfully prosecute a person.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, there are processes put in place that we need to follow.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First of all, NEA oversees a wide spectrum of enforcement offences, of which littering is one.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With such a large volume of cases and the fact that, of course, resources are not unlimited, we will have to prioritise.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The reason is because this is actually for the entire enforcement workflow, from the time we receive the feedback to investigation, to prosecuting.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When we receive the feedback, first of all, we will need at least one week to verify the information, contact the feedback provider to get witness' statement, for instance.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Then, we would need to decide if we can and should deploy camera surveillance and, if there is a positive hit, we would need to identify the flat owner, for instance, in high-rise littering, interview them as well as the suspects and we need to give a two-week notice in order to get the flat owners and the suspect to be interviewed to take statements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: All these will take about four to six weeks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is where the "10 weeks" is coming from.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But in some instances where we have very specific intelligence and very clear evidence, and it is easy to establish the identity of the suspect, for instance, we could take less than 10 weeks to clear the case.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Then, in other cases when it is complex where multiple owners are involved and where multiple rounds of surveillance cameras have to be deployed, it could take longer.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do prioritise our cases and it also depends on the urgency as well as, of course, the evidence available.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Very often, I receive replies from NEA that they carry out stakeouts when there is feedback.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But as far as I can remember, there was zero success.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Not a single time, they staked out and they managed to catch someone.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My second question is: there have been several high-rise littering of sanitary pads for many years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Because NEA deploys CCTVs only for a few days and the problem persists.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If you have a targeted ambition to catch the culprit, I am sure you would be able to catch him.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Otherwise, it looks like this problem will only disappear when the litter bug "menopauses"!

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The third question is whether NEA is short of CCTVs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And the last question: very often, my residents give feedback about their neighbours smoking along corridors, at the staircase and then, later on, littering the cigarette butts everywhere.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to stakeouts with no success, in August 2012, as I have said earlier, we started deploying surveillance cameras.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the deployment of the surveillance cameras has helped us significantly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As Members know, with stakeouts, you cannot be there 24/7.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, it really depends on intelligence from the ground for such effective stakeouts.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, the deployment of surveillance cameras is really not the panacea.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Surveillance cameras themselves obviously have some limitations, for instance, whether you can find suitable vantage points that you can put them and, of course, safeguarding the privacy of the residents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: How effective we are with the surveillance cameras also depends on the information given.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, in the case of the sanitary pad issue that the Member talked about for a specific block in Yishun, the information given to us was just a photo of the sanitary pad with no other information about where it is likely to have come from and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, for very high blocks, it is very hard, even with a surveillance camera, because we may not be able to train the cameras at the appropriate floors because the cameras do have a limit as to how many floors they can cover.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Therefore, for this particular case, we have deployed the cameras multiple times and, the last time, in August, with no results, if the Member is referring to that.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we will continue to see what we can do together.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Also, as I have said before, we cannot just depend on enforcement alone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It has to be coupled with community engagement and education.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last year, there was a pilot project which my Parliamentary colleague Ms Sun Xueling also mentioned earlier in this House, which is with Ang Mo Kio.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is a High-rise Littering/Pigeon Feeding Pilot Project that was carried out for two blocks of flats that had persistent issues with high-rise littering and pigeon feeding.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Through a combination of very proactive engagement by the grassroots organisations, together with the Town Council, NEA and the Municipal Services Office (MSO), the grassroots formed a community watch group that actually went to engage every resident in the two blocks to raise awareness about the issue.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, they are planning to roll out this programme to the rest of the Group Representation Constituency in the coming months.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As high-rise littering and pigeon feeding are human actions and require a change in mindset and behaviour, the long-term solution and a more sustainable approach must be greater community involvement, of course, facilitated or complemented by enforcement actions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On CCTVs, as I have said, resources are never unlimited.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, we will deploy surveillance cameras where it is possible and where it needs to be done.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: On the duration of deployments, as I have said, even in one of the Yishun blocks, we have deployed the cameras multiple times.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As far as the Khatib case is concerned, initially, when the CCTVs were deployed, they were actually done by the Yishun Town Council, if I am not mistaken.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We worked together with the Town Council because this is their basketball court and the problem is generally from the basketball players and there was outreach and education.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, last year, NEA came in with our own surveillance cameras and we managed to catch one last year and four this year.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to work with the Member's constituency on this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As to smoking and evidence, as I have said in my reply earlier and also in my appeal that if you do have information, whether it is video footage or photos and so on, you can submit to us.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But the feedback provider must be willing to be a witness if there is a need to be in Court.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I want to ask whether we are going to improve the surveillance cameras.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also want to share that where I stay, I do have a neighbour that was throwing cigarette butts almost every other day.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But for that week, this resident could see there was a surveillance camera, so the person did not throw any cigarette butts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The minute they removed the camera, the next day, the cigarette butts started to appear again.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, the problem might be our surveillance cameras are so big that the offenders can see them, they do not litter and that is why we do not catch anyone.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have limited cameras and they cannot be deployed all the time.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, the question is: can we improve the surveillance cameras?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said, the effectiveness has improved.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But the idea is to try and change behaviours.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, it is a longer-term solution, and we want to encourage considerate socially responsible behaviour and civic mindedness.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That should be the priority and not to catch as many people as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If the person can be rehabilitated, why not?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And if we can find something, definitely, we will look at trying it out.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: But the fact of the matter is that the Police take about 10 days to arrest the suspect.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, there must be something that they have done that can expedite this whole process.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Perhaps, NEA should look at how the Police have done it and, maybe, reduce the pain points that NEA officers have to face trying to find the culprit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier, there is a need to prioritise, depending on the public health risks and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think the Police also do the same thing.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned that I only gave the photograph of the sanitary pad.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: If this is what your staff told you, then it is not true.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I even took a photo of the stack of the windows.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, in fact, it is well-known which stack of the windows it came from.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, I would like to ask whether NEA would use deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) tests to catch the culprits.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The next question is that there are surveillance cameras in the covered basketball court at MPC@Khatib.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: How often do you view the surveillance cameras?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Recently, four have been caught because I told NEA, "Quickly go and view because it is so dirty.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: You have surveillance cameras but you never view." Then, they managed to show five pictures.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, I would like to ask how often these surveillance cameras are being viewed.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, with regard to the photos, that was what I was given to understand.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as I have also said, we have actually deployed cameras for that particular block multiple times.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Which means that, at the end of the day, we do have some idea of where the stack is and it could be additional information that the Member has given.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, if you deploy a camera for a certain period of time and you cannot catch the culprits, then obviously, you have to review whether it is the camera's positioning or whether it is the right stack or the right floor levels and so on, before you redeploy again.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And that is a process that we go through for all kinds of high-rise littering offences.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to DNA, we have answered this in Parliament before.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At least, as far as we know, the technology involved – I am not referring specifically to sanitary pads – but we are talking about in general.
